# China Property Market Profile

## Structural Characteristics
- Population: ~1.41B (declining since 2022) | Urbanization rate: ~66% (peaking)
- Housing stock: ~400M+ units (significant vacancy in lower-tier cities)
- Homeownership rate: ~90% (one of highest globally — legacy of housing reform)
- Dominant product: Off-plan (预售) sales — buyers pay before construction complete
- Key institutions: NBS (70-City Index), PBOC (mortgage policy), MOHURD (housing regulation), Local governments (land sales ~40% of revenue)

## The China Property Model — Now Broken

For 20+ years, China's economy ran on a property-industrial complex:
```
Local Govt sells land → Developer builds off-plan → Buyer pre-pays → Developer uses cash for next project
                                                                   → Local govt uses land revenue for infrastructure
                                                                   → GDP growth + jobs
```

This model broke in 2021:
- "Three Red Lines" policy (2020): Strict developer leverage caps
- Evergrande default (2021): Triggered confidence crisis
- Off-plan buyers halted purchases: "Why pay for something that might not be built?"
- Developer cash flow collapsed → cannot finish existing projects → cannot buy new land
- Local government land sales revenue collapsed (-30-50% in many cities)

## Historical Cycle Phases

| Period | Phase | Key Driver |
|--------|-------|------------|
| 1998-2003 | Early boom | Housing privatization reform |
| 2004-2008 | Boom | Urbanization, export-led growth |
| 2009-2010 | Surge | 4 Trillion RMB stimulus |
| 2011-2015 | Boom + correction cycles | Policy oscillation (tighten → loosen) |
| 2015-2018 | Mega-boom | Shantytown renovation (棚改), PSL lending, monetary easing |
| 2019-2021 | Peak | Three Red Lines, COVID, developer stress begins |
| 2021-2025 | Structural Bust | Evergrande, Country Garden, cascading developer defaults |
| 2025-? | Stabilization attempt | Government bailouts, "whitelist" projects, rate cuts |

## Key China-Specific Drivers

### 1. Three Red Lines (2020) — The Policy That Broke the Cycle
| Red Line | Threshold | Purpose |
|----------|----------|---------|
| Liability/Asset Ratio > 70% | Excluding pre-sale proceeds | Limit leverage |
| Net Debt/Equity > 100% | Excluding pre-sale proceeds | Limit debt |
| Cash/Short-Term Debt < 1.0× | — | Ensure liquidity |

Developers were given until 2023 to comply. Most couldn't. The policy was simultaneously too effective (broke the model) and not effective enough (too late).

### 2. The Off-Plan (预售) Problem
- ~80-90% of new home sales are off-plan (buyers pay 1-3 years before delivery)
- Developer uses buyer deposits to fund construction (in effect, buyers are unsecured creditors)
- When developers can't finish → "rotten tail" (烂尾) projects
- Estimated 20-40% of off-plan projects delayed or stalled
- Mortgage strike movement (2022): Buyers refused to pay mortgages on undelivered homes

### 3. The Oversupply Problem
- Tier 1 cities (Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Guangzhou): Land scarcity, structurally undersupplied
- Tier 2 cities (Hangzhou, Nanjing, Chengdu, Wuhan): Mixed — some oversupplied
- Tier 3/4 cities: Massive oversupply, "ghost cities," population declining
- National vacancy rate estimated 15-25% (vs 5-10% in DM)
- 50-100M vacant units estimated

### 4. Housing as Store of Wealth
- Property = ~60-70% of Chinese household wealth (vs ~30-40% in DM)
- No alternative investment options (capital controls, underdeveloped capital markets)
- Housing is the primary savings vehicle for the middle class
- Price decline = direct wealth destruction for majority of population
- This makes sustained house price decline uniquely politically sensitive

### 5. Demographics — Structural Headwind
- Working-age population declining since 2014
- Total population declining since 2022
- New household formation decelerating
- Long-term housing demand: 800M-1.2B m²/year (declining from 1.5B+ m² peak)
- This is a permanent structural shift, not cyclical

## Key Data Sources

| Data | Source | Frequency | Notes |
|------|--------|----------|-------|
| 70-City New Home Price Index | NBS | Monthly | Most cited, but may overstate (excludes discounts) |
| 70-City Secondary Price Index | NBS | Monthly | Better indicator of market sentiment |
| Property Sales (floor space) | NBS | Monthly | Volume is key — price follows volume |
| New Construction Starts | NBS | Monthly | Leading indicator of developer activity |
| Real Estate Investment | NBS | Monthly | Fixed asset investment in property |
| Land Sales Revenue | MOF | Monthly | Key local government fiscal indicator |
| Developer Funding Sources | NBS | Monthly | Shows which funding channels are open/closed |

## Tier System

| Tier | Cities | Population (each) | Price Level | Current Status |
|------|--------|------------------|------------|---------------|
| Tier 1 | Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Guangzhou | 15-25M | ¥50-80K/m² | Stabilizing (scarcity) |
| New Tier 1 | Hangzhou, Chengdu, Wuhan, Nanjing, etc. (~15) | 8-18M | ¥15-30K/m² | Mixed recovery |
| Tier 2 | Provincial capitals, major cities (~30) | 3-10M | ¥8-15K/m² | Still declining |
| Tier 3/4 | Smaller cities, county-level (~200+) | < 3M | ¥3-8K/m² | Worst — excess supply + population loss |

## Policy Response (2021-2025)

| Policy | Date | Impact |
|--------|------|--------|
| Three Red Lines relaxed | 2022 | Too late — developer confidence already destroyed |
| Mortgage rate cuts (LPR 5Y) | 2022-2024 | Reduced from 4.65% to 3.95% — modest stimulus |
| Down payment reductions | 2023-2024 | Tier 1: 30% → 20%, Tier 2: 20% → 15% |
| "Whitelist" project financing | 2024 | ~$50B allocated to finish stalled projects |
| Home purchase restrictions removed | 2024 | Most cities removed all buying restrictions |
| Government buying unsold homes | 2024 | PBOC relending facility for SOE purchases |

## Key Risks

### Downside
- Developer defaults continue (estimated 50%+ of developers face insolvency)
- Price decline accelerates → household wealth destruction → consumption collapse
- Local government fiscal crisis (land revenue collapse, LGFV debt ~$9T)
- Banking system: property loans ~25-30% of bank assets + LGFV exposure
- Deflationary spiral: falling prices → delayed purchases → more falling prices

### Upside
- Aggressive PBOC stimulus (RRR cuts, MLF cuts, PSL, direct purchases)
- Fiscal bazooka: central government takes over local government property debts
- Urban village redevelopment program (new cycle of demolition + relocation)
- Household savings rate is high (~35%) — spending power exists if confidence returns

### Cycle Assessment
- Phase: Structural Bust → Attempted Stabilization
- Unlike any other major property cycle globally — this is a MODEL change, not just a cycle
- Key question: Can China transition from property-driven growth to consumption/technology-driven growth without a crisis?
- Local government fiscal model (40% revenue from land sales) must be rebuilt
